messages:
alex (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock ordering for the OptKit lift: quantization, batching, caching. Customer asks, enterprise ROI asks, and our sprint slots are tight. Can we pick a sequence and landing criteria today?

maya (Eng): My vote: batching first. Biggest immediate latency wins for conversational workloads and relatively small infra changes.

ryan (ML): Leaning quant-first for cost-per-token. Quantization can drop 30-50% perf cost for some of our models. Risk: model quality regressions and more eval work.

sophia (SRE): Caching is lowest-risk operationally — prefix/KV cache can be toggled per-route and gives cost & p95 wins for common prompts. But it doesn't help tail-latency for new inputs.

luis (Design): From a UX POV we want deterministic behavior. Caching changes user-visible latencies; need signal in the API or sticky session fallback if we evict.

alex (PM): Helpful. To force a decision I sketched quick RICE-ish numbers for the three:
```
Quantization: Reach=High (all token calls), Impact=High (cost), Confidence=Medium, Effort=Large -> score ~ 6.
Batching: Reach=Medium (concurrent workloads), Impact=Medium (latency/cost), Confidence=High, Effort=Medium -> score ~ 7.
Caching: Reach=Low-Medium (repeated prefixes), Impact=Low-Medium, Confidence=High, Effort=Small -> score ~ 8.
```
Numbers are fuzzy but show caching is high ROI per effort, batching next, quantization is highest impact but largest effort.

ryan (ML): I agree on the framing. Suggest parallel paths: 1) ship caching as a quick feature flag experiment with customer opt-in; 2) schedule batching as the main sprint deliverable; 3) run quantization as a cross-team project with an internal beta. That preserves velocity and reduces regression risk.

maya (Eng): Implementation notes: batching needs runtime changes (dynamic batching + backpressure). I can scope an MVP that supports per-route batch windows and a safety timeout. ETA: 3 sprints for robust.

sophia (SRE): For caching we can add an opt-in prefix cache behind a feature flag, expose cache hit metrics in the Console, and set default TTLs per-customer. Ops effort: small.

luis (Design): I'll draft copy for docs and the Console UX for cache opt-in, and a short explainer for potential consistency caveats.

alex (PM): Launch criteria proposal:
- Caching: feature-flagged opt-in, cache-hit ratio > 20% for pilot customers, no regressions in correctness tests.
- Batching: p95 latency <= baseline + 10% for single-user flows, throughput uplift >= 1.5x for high-concurrency workloads.
- Quantization: token-cost reduction >= 25% on validated models with quality delta < 1% on core evals.

alex (PM): Decision call: ship caching this sprint (opt-in), prioritize batching for next sprint (MVP), run quantization as a tracked project with milestones for evals + rollout. Anyone blocking?

maya (Eng): Not blocking. Will put batching epic in sprint backlog and add scope notes.

ryan (ML): Not blocking. I'll start model-specific quant experiments and share evaluation harness next week.

sophia (SRE): Not blocking. I'll add metrics + dashboard hooks and a deploy plan for cache flag.

luis (Design): Not blocking. Will drop initial UX mock and doc PR today.

deploy-bot: alex (PM) requested a reminder: "optkit-ordering-playbook" check-in scheduled for 1902580000.

alex (PM): Great — we'll re-evaluate RICE after we have first cache pilot metrics. Thanks all :thumbsup:
